chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bazanty, from Jamil, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

In how many items is alms-tax due? He said: In nine things which God's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) established, and forgave tax on what is besides that. Al-Tayyar said: We have a grain called rice? He said to him: We also have much grain. He asked him: Is there anything due on it? He said: Did I not tell you that God's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) forgave tax on what is besides that? Among them are gold and silver, and three from animals: camels, sheep, and cows, and from what the earth produces: wheat, barley, raisins, and dates.
ai.seo_question: What are the nine specific items on which zakat is obligatory according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Khisal highlights the principle of 'tawfiq' (divine facilitation) in zakat, where the Prophet specified nine primary categories while exempting others like rice, reflecting the practical realities of 7th-century Arabia. Shaykh al-Saduq uses this to demonstrate the fixed nature of these obligations, a view supported by many Shia jurists who distinguish between these specific assets and other wealth subject to different rules. The dialogue with al-Tayyar underscores the prophetic authority in defining the scope of obligatory alms, preventing arbitrary expansion of the tax burden.
